chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Safwan from Al-'Iyyas ibn Al-Qasim said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the woman enter into the state of Ihram while she is menstruating? He said: 'Yes, she performs Ghusl and says Talbiyah.'
And the Istihadah woman (one with irregular bleeding) does what is obligatory upon her, then she enters Ihram at the Miqat. Narrated.

key_terms.تُحْرِمُ: Enters the state of Ihram (sacred ritual status)
key_terms.عِنْدَ الْمِيقَاتِ: At the Miqat (ritual boundary/place of entry)
key_terms.وَالْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: The woman with Istihadah (irregular uterine bleeding)

ai.seo_question: When should a menstruating woman enter Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Iss ibn Qasim, transmitted via Safwan, clarifies that menstruating and Istihadah women enter Ihram immediately upon reaching the Miqat after performing Ghusl and reciting the Talbiyah, without waiting for complete purity. This ruling highlights the distinction between the state of Ihram (a contractual status) and the state of ritual purity required for specific acts like prayer, a key principle in Shia fiqh. It underscores the practical ease granted to women during Hajj, allowing them to assume the sacred state even while in a state of major impurity.
